raptor.title: Log locations and retention

requirement_statement.text: Definitions: sc-agent is the crates and CLIs of this repository. A CLI is one of the command-line programs decidr or sitr; `<cli>` is its name in lower case and `<CLI>` in upper case. A Logger is an sc-observability logger that a caller passes to a CLI's library entry point. The general log is the diagnostic log of one entry point (ADR-SAG-0021); decidr's is `decidr.log.jsonl` and sitr's is `sitr.log.jsonl`. A session log is the record of every session; a session is one model request with its own ULID `session_id`, and every send of that request, including busy resends, belongs to it. A link record ties one run to one session (REQ-SAG-0005). A run log is the file of link records that sits beside a session log in the same directory. To remove a log is to rotate, prune or delete it. The generated client is the Python module a consumer renders from the sc-decidr wheel's sc-compose template (REQ-SAG-0018). The client name is the consumer's product name, a constant in the generated client, and equals its `agent_role` (REQ-SAG-0004), such as `plan-anchor` or `judge-jev`. The client Logger is the Logger the generated client obtains from the wheel under the client name (REQ-SAG-0008). `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is the environment variable named by the client name uppercased with hyphens replaced by underscores. The default session files are the session files REQ-SAG-0005 names for an agent role. The client's logs are the general log the client Logger writes and the default session files.

statements.text: With no Logger injected, each CLI MUST write its general log to `~/.sc-agent/logs/<cli>.log.jsonl`.
When `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` is set and non-empty, that CLI MUST use its value in place of `~/.sc-agent`.
When `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is set and not empty, the generated client MUST use that folder in place of `~/.sc-agent/` for its logs.

requirement_statement.text: Definitions: A busy response is a non-quota HTTP 429, 502 or 529. A send is one transmission of a request; all sends of one request belong to one session. The holdoff is the time a busy request waits before it is resent. `Retry-After` is the HTTP response header that gives that time in seconds. statements.text: A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
A request whose send has a network failure MUST be resent unchanged, counting toward the same maximum number of sends.
The maximum number of sends per request MUST be a configurable maximum, 5 by default.
When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.
Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.
When the provider gives a `Retry-After`, it MUST set the holdoff.
When the provider gives no `Retry-After`, the holdoffs MUST back off exponentially; this requirement does not fix their values.
A held-off request MUST wait in the queue until its holdoff ends, and the wait MUST end at once when the request is cancelled.
When sends run out on busy replies, the error MUST say busy, with the send count.
Authentication (401) and quota MUST NOT be resent; they MUST be returned with the remote error id and message.

raptor.rationale:
Providers signal overload with busy responses and expect clients to back off. Holding off in the queue keeps workers free and lets cancellation take effect immediately.

A busy provider is busy for every worker; one worker's holdoff that the others ignore only multiplies the busy replies.

raptor.title: sc-decidr is the one Python decision harness

context.text:
sc-decidr is the harness through which sc-agent's Python consumers reach decision models (Jev, decider, Laya, Haiku, Luna). The owner requires judge-jev, plan-anchor and every later consumer to integrate identically for errors, API keys, model selection, the injectable general logger and session logging, differing only in prompt authoring and result handling.

The two existing consumers each rebuilt the wheel boundary, and the copies diverged: judge-jev pins an id list with a `JEV.UNMAPPED` fallback while plan-anchor matches message text (`"http 401"`); plan-anchor pins `provider="typesafe"`, disabling Haiku and Luna; both re-sort `send_batch` results; judge-jev refuses `--timeout` while plan-anchor calls the unreleased `timeout_secs`. Consumers had no category to branch on and no per-call worker count or timeout.

decision.text:
The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3.

1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path.

   **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`, shipped as package data; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged.

   - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping.
   - model selectors are Run arguments.
   - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path.
   - Python results are typed values, not dicts.
   - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced.

   **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library.

2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601).

5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016).

6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop.

7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules.

8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702).

11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request.

14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

rationale.text: Two consumers rebuilt the boundary and diverged, so the boundary moves into the wheel and integration code is generated from one template. A stored category and the send count replace message parsing and pinned id lists, and per-run limits and position-tagged results remove consumer workarounds.

positive: Every Python consumer renders the same integration module and holds only its prompts and result handling.
No consumer parses error text or pins id lists, and all Jev data takes one session-log path.
negative: The wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout.

raptor.title: Configuration has a shared scope and one scope per CLI, each global and per worktree

context.text:
sc-agent ships two CLIs today, `decidr` and `sitr`. CLI launchers for other agent harnesses, such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Hermes and pi-agent, will be added as their peers. Apps such as plan-anchor and judge-jev wrap a CLI the way a named agent (`.claude/agents/<agent>.md`) wraps a harness. Agent-level settings, for agents such as `lai`, `sai`, `sanity`, `plan-anchor` and `judge-jev`, will later be provided by the CLI launchers.

Before this decision, every CLI read one shared file pair, `~/.sc-agent/default.json` and `~/.sc-agent/local.json`, with `SC_AGENT__<KEY>` environment overrides. That layout has no per-CLI settings and no per-repository layer: two worktrees of one repository cannot hold different settings, and a setting meant for one CLI applies to all of them.
context.problem_statement: Each CLI needs its own settings, shared defaults may be overridden by a CLI file, and a repository or worktree must be able to override both.

key_principles: A narrower location beats a wider one: local beats global.
Within one location, a CLI's own file beats the shared file.
sc ecosystem files in a repository live under `.sc/`, so a repository needs one `.gitignore` entry rather than one per tool.

rationale.text:
One file per CLI keeps each CLI's settings separate and lets a new CLI be added without touching another CLI's file. The shared file gives one place for shared defaults that a CLI file may override. The local location under `.sc/` lets each worktree differ, which matters because worktrees of one repository often work on different phases at the same time. Env vars named after the CLI keep one CLI's override from reaching another.

raptor.title: One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

context.text: sc-agent logs through sc-observability. The `decidr` CLI, the `sitr` CLI and the sc-decidr wheel already link the sc-observability crate. Two kinds of log exist: the general log (diagnostics, searched for issues) and session logs (the long-term record of every successful model query and its response, analysed later and loaded into SQLite, ADR-SAG-0002).
context.problem_statement: Every general-log record of a process must reach one Logger that the process's entry point owns, and every log must land at a fixed, known path, with session logs never mixed with general logs.

decision.text:
**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`.

**The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** The sc-decidr wheel returns the sc-observability crate's `Logger` to Python, named by the caller. Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. The wheel has no dependency on the `sc-observability` Python package.

**Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product.

| Product | Contains |
|---|---|
| `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability |
| `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability |
| sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability |

There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses.

**Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged, so with nothing configured every log lands under `~/.sc-agent/` for a full audit. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility.

**Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink.

**Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root: its `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` environment override when set and non-empty (used by tests), else `~/.sc-agent`. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004).

- Session logs are `~/.sc-agent/sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl`, and each one's run log is `runs.jsonl` in the same directory.

| Entry point | General log | Session logs |
|---|---|---|
| `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |
| `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none |
| `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |
| `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |

A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added.

**Session identity.**

- `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting.
- `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14).
- `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase".

**Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.
key_principles: One process, one general Logger, one queue, owned by the entry point; session rows and link records go through sc-agent's session sink, never the general Logger.
Session logs and general logs are never written to the same folder tree.
A session is never filed under a guessed project/phase.

rationale.text: The entry point is the only code that knows the process's lifetime, so it is the only correct owner of the Logger: it obtains the Logger before the first general-log record and flushes after each call. Exposing the crate's own Logger from the wheel keeps one copy and one queue in the process and needs no Python package. Fixed paths keep every log in one known place for audit, and a separate `sessions/` tree lets tools and the later SQLite load read every session with a path glob. The session log is the record of every successful Jev query from every tool, so it cannot be turned off and is never rotated; it stays small enough because `project` changes over time.

positive: Libraries hold no logging policy: they take a Logger or use the default.
`sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/` selects one agent's work in one phase with a path glob.
negative: Every caller must supply a project/phase before its first request.

The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3.

1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path.

   **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`, shipped as package data; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged.

   - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping.
   - model selectors are Run arguments.
   - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path.
   - Python results are typed values, not dicts.
   - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced.

   **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library.

2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601).

5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016).

6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop.
